82557bfe: Optimum makes blockchain data move faster between the machines that run a network. Its first product, mump2p, gets each new Ethereum block to validators sooner than the default route does.
301f24a5: It does not change Ethereum itself. Operators run a small extra program next to their node, and blocks start arriving earlier.
3bfe56a3: Why a few hundred milliseconds matter
497f6fa1: Ethereum makes a block every 12 seconds, and validators have to vote on it quickly. A validator that sees the block late can miss the vote or vote on the wrong thing, and that costs rewards. Across a market of staked ETH worth around 100 billion dollars, small delays add up.
693d92a4: That is the idea behind the slogan the team uses: speed is money.
4b9a8c53: How it works, without the math
a56222b0: Normally a block travels as a whole, passed from peer to peer, and every peer waits for the full copy before sending it on.
899d4cdf: mump2p cuts the block into pieces and mixes them into coded pieces with a technique called Random Linear Network Coding (RLNC). Think of each coded piece as one equation about the block: once a node holds enough independent equations, from any senders in any order, it can solve for the whole block. Nodes in the middle can also mix fresh pieces from what they already hold, without waiting for the full block.
fafbdf32: An operator runs a gateway: one container on a host next to the beacon node. The gateway acts as a peer of the consensus client and never receives validator keys. Prysm, Lighthouse, Teku, Nimbus and Lodestar are supported, and the usual gossip route keeps running alongside it, so the gateway adds a faster path instead of replacing one.
1b7a0464: People without validators will be able to run a stream only gateway and serve the block stream to their own apps, once Optimum turns on consumer tokens for every account.
c7b4cea0: Signal hands blocks from the Optimum mesh to your beacon node so your validators receive them sooner. It is free for Ethereum validators: operators sign up in the Console, start the gateway, and Optimum switches Signal on for the account.
c78a06ce: Accelerate goes further for large operators: it recommends a bid cutoff for the MEV sidecar they already run, based on the slots their validators proposed. It needs at least 200 active mainnet validators and has to be enabled by Optimum.
8d647848: Flexnodes are extra nodes that add bandwidth and shorten distances in the network. They receive block data through a gateway and send more coded pieces to the validators that need them. Operators would be paid through a Latency Marketplace, where validators pay for the pieces they need.
afb36512: The early rollout is limited to existing validator partners, with wider community participation planned after testing.
2a77e6fe: What the evidence says so far
e0b21f05: Optimum's own figures, published live on its Hub, show blocks reaching nodes faster than the default gossip route in most slots. Outside checks are more mixed: Lido’s PERCH evaluation on the Hoodi testnet found blocks arriving about 407 ms sooner at the 95th percentile and wrong head votes down 45%, while an independent StereumLabs study on 36 mainnet nodes with an early gateway build found some clients faster and none statistically significant. Optimum replied that its network-wide acceleration was switched on during that study, which blurred the comparison.

c057129f: Optimum switched on mump2p for Ethereum on 20 October 2026. At launch 16 node operators ran it, with about 22,000 validator keys and more than 1.4 million staked ETH behind them. e72eff43: Gateway v1.3.5: operators on v1.3.2 or v1.3.3 should upgrade
76ab1e43: Optimum released gateway v1.3.5 on 16 November. The release notes say v1.3.2 and v1.3.3 are no longer supported because they contained security vulnerabilities, and v1.3.4 users should upgrade for CVE-2026-78661. The release also rejects oversized consensus requests, stops beacon nodes from asking the gateway for data columns it never serves, and lets a configured consensus peer reconnect after a disconnect. No configuration change is needed.
cbb9b18f: Outside tests: one clear gain, one inconclusive
4ef41de2: Lido's PERCH evaluation ran on the Hoodi testnet from 17 September to 15 October with six operators and 267 qualifying keys. Over 180,327 slots, the 95th percentile block arrival fell from 1,614 ms to 1,207 ms, 407 ms sooner, and wrong head votes fell 45% against a June control week. Lido's own summary warns that Hoodi is small and noisy, so the results are directional rather than a mainnet forecast, and Lido has not yet announced a decision. Earlier, a StereumLabs study of 36 mainnet full nodes with an early gateway build saw Lighthouse about 120 ms and Prysm about 60 ms earlier, Teku flat and Nimbus slower, with nothing statistically significant. Optimum replied that its network-wide acceleration was on during that study, which blurred the comparison.
efc72baa: Vitalik names erasure coded networking as a useful upgrade
062231a9: In a 9 November post about Ethereum's roadmap, Vitalik Buterin listed erasure coded peer to peer networking for large data objects as a useful improvement, with implementation complexity as the main tradeoff. He did not name Optimum. The same day Muriel Médard posted that this is the networking improvement her team has built; his proposals and mump2p are separate, but they come from the same family of ideas.
